title: Determination of neopterin and biopterin by liquid chromatography coupled to tandem mass spectrometry \(LC-MS/MS) in rat and human plasma, cell extracts and tissue homogenates
protocol: Collect blood into two heparinized tubes for unstimulated control and forskolin.
Add forskolin stock to one tube to achieve a final concentration of 10 μM.
Incubate both samples at 37°C for 24 hours.
Centrifuge the samples in a tabletop centrifuge at 3000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Store plasma at -80°C.
Euthanize and debleed animals, rapidly excise DRGs and spinal cord tissue.
Immediately freeze tissues on dry ice or liquid nitrogen.
Store frozen tissues at -80°C.
Add 200 μl of 0.1 M hydrochloric acid containing 20 ng/ml internal standard rhamnopterin to defrosted tissue samples in a microcentrifuge tube.
Homogenize tissue with reusable pellet pestles for 45 seconds, ensuring at least 10 strokes.
Remove 10 μl of suspension for protein determination.
Add 100 μl of fresh iodine solution (1% w/v iodine and 2% w/v potassium iodide in 1 M hydrochloric acid) to the homogenized tissue.
Mix thoroughly and incubate in darkness at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Stop reaction by adding 200 μl of freshly prepared ascorbic acid solution (5% w/v).
Vortex mixture until decolorization occurs.
Activate the cation-exchange cartridge with 1 ml methanol.
Activate the cation-exchange cartridge with 1 ml water.
Load the completely decolorized sample onto the cartridge.
Vacuum elute unbound substances at a speed of 1 ml per minute.
Wash the cartridge with 1 ml 0.1 M hydrochloric acid.
Wash the cartridge with 1 ml methanol.
Elute bound substances with 1 ml of 8% ammonia solution in 25% methanol.
Evaporate the organic solvent to dryness using a gentle stream of nitrogen at 40°C.
Reconstitute the residue with 200 μl water/0.002% formic acid.
Transfer the reconstituted solution into a screw vial with a glass insert and Silikon/PTFE seals in the screw cap.
Use a Gemini C18 column for chromatographic separation.
Connect the Gemini C18 column to a pump and autosampler.
Use water with 0.002% formic acid as mobile phase eluent A.
Use methanol with 0.002% formic acid as mobile phase eluent B.
Apply a gradient from 100:0 to 5:95 over 3.5 minutes starting at 0.5 min.
Maintain the ratio of 5:95 for 3 minutes after reaching the gradient.
Apply a gradient from 5:95 to 100:0 over 1 minute starting at 7 min.
Maintain the ratio of 100:0 for 5 minutes after reaching the final gradient.
Inject 10 μl of the sample onto the LC-MS/MS.
Set the flow rate to 0.3 ml/min.
Set the runtime to 13 min.
Choose the negative ion mode with an electrospray voltage of -4300 V at 400 °C.
Set the auxiliary and nebulizer gas to 50 psi.
Set the curtain gas to 10 psi.
Set the collision gas to 5 psi.
Use pure nitrogen as gases.
Use precursor-to-product ion transitions of m/z 236 to 192 for biopterin with a collision energy of -20 V.
Use precursor-to-product ion transitions of m/z 252 to 192 for neopterin with a collision energy of -22 V.
Use precursor-to-product ion transitions of m/z 265 to 192 for rhamnopterin with a collision energy of -20 V.
Set the dwell time to 150 ms for multiple reaction monitoring (MRM).
Evaluate concentrations of samples using calibration standards ranging from 0.1 to 50 ng/ml.
Use Analyst software 1.4 (Applied Biosystems) for evaluation.
Insert a quality control sample every tenth sample during each run at concentrations of 1, 10, or 50 ng/ml.
